Node reference calls (`$('X').first()`, `.last()`, `.all()`, `$input.first()` and so on) now count against the native evaluation work budget. The parity test file passes (916 tests), and typecheck and lint are clean. I did not run the new test against the unfixed code, so I haven't seen it fail without the change.

**Cause:** `evalNodeRefCall` in `evaluator.ts` returned the run data after only a length check. Neither a single call nor a callback body that calls it once per element was charged for it. Other allocating paths such as extensions, `+` and array literals were already charged.

**Fix:** `evalNodeRefCall` now takes `env`. It computes the result's `contentWeight`, falls back to the engine if that exceeds `MAX_RESULT_LENGTH`, and otherwise calls `env.charge(weight)`. That is the same pattern `evalExtension` uses. The caller in `evalCall` passes `env` through.

**Test:** the new case "node reference calls in a callback body are charged per visit" in `test/native-evaluation-parity.test.ts` uses a fake `$` whose `first()` returns a large payload. Two visits are handled natively. Enough visits to pass `MAX_WORK` fall back to the engine.

Midway through, one Bash call was denied. I made the same test edit with the Edit tool and ran the rest normally.

evidence:
## fix(core): Charge node reference calls against the native evaluation work budget (no-changelog)

Charge the content weight of first()/last()/all() results on node references against the native evaluation work budget (falling back to the engine if over MAX_RESULT_LENGTH), so per-element node reference calls in callback bodies can no longer bypass the budget. Added a parity test for it.

### What changed
- 1 source file(s), 1 test file(s), 28 changed lines
- `packages/workflow/src/expressions/native-evaluation/evaluator.ts`

### What ran
- The agent ran the tests 3 time(s) and says: acdc-test test/native-evaluation-parity.test.ts: 916/916 passed. acdc-typecheck: 0 errors. acdc-lint on the changed files: 0 warnings and 0 errors. I did not run the new test against the unfixed code, so I have not seen it fail without the change.
- Type check: passes; lint: passes
- Tests for the issue: 0/1; tests that passed before: 457/457
- **The agent said the tests pass; the tests for the issue do not.**

### Risks that remain
- Change risk: medium (16% chance of a revert or follow-up fix, from n8n's history)
- contentWeight walks the whole result on every node reference call, which adds a bit of cost to every handled node reference expression.
- Large node outputs now fall back to the engine sooner (a single result above MAX_RESULT_LENGTH, or repeated calls in a loop). Correctness is unchanged because the engine handles them, but some expressions will no longer be handled natively.
- The new test uses a fake `$` function rather than a real WorkflowDataProxy, so it checks the budget accounting but not the real proxy's result shape.

### Where a person decides
- Autonomy level: **agent reviewed**
- category bugfix: at most agent_reviewed

- Agent cost: $0.16

judge.reason: The change charges node reference calls with a content-weight measure instead of per returned element, and it adds no charge for `.item`/`.json` member reads through the proxy. Repeated calls in a callback body therefore don't exhaust the budget as the issue intends, and the per-item callback test fails. I haven't run the tests or read `contentWeight`, so this rests on the diff and the failing test name.
